# Purr

> Purr is free, open-source (MIT) dictation, meeting notes and voice editing for macOS on Apple silicon. Hold a key, speak, and your words appear in whichever app has focus. Everything runs on your Mac: your voice is never sent to a server, and it works offline once its models have downloaded.

- Hotkeys: hold Right Option to dictate (or tap to start and stop), Control-Option-M for meetings, Control-Option-E for Voice Edit. Each has a few other keys to pick from in Settings.
- Engines: Parakeet TDT v2 (default, English) and WhisperKit (about 100 languages, auto-detected or pinned, with optional translation to English).
- Smart Typing: with Parakeet, words appear in the app while you are still talking (English only).
- Meetings: an AI notetaker with no bot in the call. It records your mic and your Mac's system audio (macOS 14.2+), labels speakers (also when only the mic hears them), saves transcripts as Markdown with optional audio, and, with summaries turned on, writes one in the meeting's language. English and 27 more languages.
- Voice Edit: select text, hold the key and say what to change. Apple Intelligence (macOS 26) or Gemma 4 E2B rewrites it on your Mac.
- Vocabulary: names and terms that dictation listens for, fixes for words it keeps mishearing, voice commands ("comma", "new paragraph", "scratch that") and filler-word trimming.
- Speed: text appears 0.22 s after the key is released, against 0.63 s for Wispr Flow and 1.30 s for Superwhisper on the same recordings.
- Privacy: no telemetry, no account. Purr goes online only to download models (Parakeet is about 450 MB) and, if you allow it, to check GitHub for updates once a day.
- Updates: each update shows its release notes first, and its signature is checked before it replaces the app.
- Requirements: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later on Apple silicon. Intel Macs are not supported.
- Price: free. Source code: https://github.com/iamarunbrahma/purr
- Made by Arun Brahma, an independent developer. Contact: contact@arunbrahma.com
